findings.F1: The book loses on the day right after the rise. Across all 8848 active bars, the coin's next-day return minus its own mean is -0.154% (t -3.01). This holds at every forecast size, from -0.18% in the 0-2 bucket to -0.36% in the 15-20 bucket. Yet the book's position is largest on exactly that day, rising from 0.02 to 0.90 as the forecast grows.
findings.F2: The carry the verdict found arrives only on days 2 to 5 after the rise. In the 15-20 bucket the mean coin return is +0.30% on day 3 and +0.34% on day 4, after -0.36% excess on day 1. The 5-day return of the 6-10 and above buckets (+0.44% to +0.51%) sits only about at the coins' unconditional 5-day mean (+0.43% in the 0 bucket).
findings.F3: Volume separates the two parts of the move. After rises in the top volume tercile (volume against its prior 20-day average), the next day is flat (-0.02% excess, t -0.20) and days 2 to 5 carry on (+0.54% excess, t 2.72, n 2713). After rises in the bottom tercile, the next day reverses (-0.22%, t -2.58) and days 2 to 5 also lose (-0.14%, t -0.75).
findings.F4: Fees exceed the gross gain. The position changes on 54% of days (mean absolute change 0.34 of the book), and the per-bar fee shares sum to 6.42 against summed gross position gains of 4.39. Three of six coins (LTC, ETH, XMR) have a negative mean daily book return, down to -0.068% for XMR.
findings.F5: The book misses the market's rise. Its mean position is 0.23 and it is long on only 43% of bars, while the coins rose +0.12% a day on average. Every coin's book mean daily return (-0.068% to +0.036%) is far below its coin's (+0.067% to +0.155%), so Sharpe minus holding's Sharpe is -0.72.
findings.F6: The carry on days 2 to 5 depends on the market's direction. Their mean excess return after rises was -1.44% in 2018 and -0.88% in 2022, against +1.98% in 2020 and +0.87% in 2021.

ideas.idea: When a coin rises over one day by more than its usual daily move (its 20-day volatility), it gives part back on the next day and then keeps rising over the following 4 days. The larger the rise in units of that volatility and the heavier that day's volume against its 20-day average volume, the larger this further rise from the second to the fifth day.
ideas.consequence: Lean long on a sharp up day only after its first day has passed, with conviction growing with both the size of the rise and its volume, instead of buying at the close of the up day itself.
ideas.name: heavy-volume rises carry later

ideas.idea: When a coin rises over one day by more than its usual daily move (its 20-day volatility) on volume lighter than its 20-day average volume, it falls over the next day. The lighter that day's volume against its average, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A sharp up day on thin volume is a reason to fade it for one day rather than follow it.
ideas.name: thin-volume rises reverse next day

ideas.idea: When a coin rises over one day by more than its usual daily move (its 20-day volatility), it keeps rising over the next 5 days, only while the coin's own 60-day return is positive. The larger the rise in units of that volatility, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: Follow sharp up days only in a coin that is itself trending up, and refuse them in a falling coin.
ideas.name: sharp rises carry in uptrends
